title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Explore the key streets and corridors in Vestal and Downtown Binghamton that define the off-campus experience for students.

cards.title: University Plaza
cards.subtitle: Vestal Parkway East
cards.notes: Visit this shopping hub directly across from campus for student essentials like Five Guys, Moghul Fine Indian Cuisine, and Tully's Good Times.
cards.short_summary: A primary commercial plaza located on the Vestal Parkway directly adjacent to the main university entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: University Plaza features several smaller stores and restaurants, including Five Guys Burgers and Fries, Moghul Fine Indian Cuisine, and Tully's.
cards.access_notes: Open daily for retail and dining; easily accessible via the campus pedestrian bridge.

cards.title: University Downtown Center
cards.subtitle: Washington Street
cards.notes: Attend classes or visit the CCPA Dean's Office at this dedicated academic block in the heart of the city's urban core.
cards.short_summary: Binghamton University's primary academic facility in downtown Binghamton, housing the College of Community and Public Affairs.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Downtown Center is located at 67 Washington Street and houses the CCPA Dean's Office and various academic programs.
cards.access_notes: Academic building hours typically follow the university schedule; student ID may be required for after-hours access.

cards.title: 205 Dry
cards.subtitle: State Street
cards.notes: Experience a themed dining atmosphere at this speakeasy-style restaurant known for its curated dinner menu and vintage decor.
cards.short_summary: A popular downtown restaurant on State Street offering a unique speakeasy aesthetic and full dinner service.
cards.evidence_claim: 205 Dry is located at 205 State St and offers a thoughtfully developed dinner program within an intimate setting.
cards.source_title: 205 Dry | Speakeasy Cocktail Bar in Downtown Binghamton
cards.access_notes: Open for dinner starting at 5 PM; reservations are highly recommended.

cards.title: 20 Hawley
cards.subtitle: Hawley Street
cards.notes: Study in the on-site Tech Center or grab a coffee at the Signature JOE Coffee Bar in this major student residential block.
cards.short_summary: A large-scale off-campus student housing complex that serves as a central hub for downtown student life.
cards.evidence_claim: 20 Hawley features a Tech Center, Signature JOE Coffee Bar, and is located between Washington and State streets.
cards.access_notes: Residential complex; common areas and coffee bar access may be restricted to residents and guests.

cards.title: The Printing House
cards.subtitle: Chenango Street
cards.notes: Live in the heart of downtown at this converted historic building, located just one block from the city's main transit lines.
cards.short_summary: A prominent student housing facility on Chenango Street known for its central location and modern amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: The Printing House is located at 19 Chenango Street and offers student housing near the downtown core.
cards.source_title: The Printing House | Student Housing in Binghamton
cards.access_notes: Leasing office open Monday through Saturday; residential access for tenants only.

cards.title: Court Street Corridor
cards.subtitle: Court Street
cards.notes: Walk this central downtown thoroughfare to reach the Broome County Courthouse and various local eateries and shops.
cards.short_summary: A major commercial and civic street in downtown Binghamton frequently used by students living off-campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Court Street is a short walk to the University Downtown Center and the Broome County Courthouse.
cards.access_notes: Public street with 24/7 sidewalk access; business hours vary by establishment.

cards.title: West Side District
cards.subtitle: Main Street
cards.notes: Explore the historic West Side, where many students reside in Victorian-era homes and frequent local neighborhood businesses.
cards.short_summary: A residential and commercial district on the West Side of Binghamton popular for off-campus student living.
cards.evidence_claim: Binghamton University students most often live in Downtown Binghamton or on the West Side off Main Street.
cards.access_notes: Public residential district; served by frequent OCCT bus routes to campus.

cards.title: Transportation Center
cards.subtitle: Henry Street
cards.notes: Catch a bus to campus or other regional destinations at this central transit hub located on the edge of downtown.
cards.short_summary: The primary hub for local and regional bus services, including Broome County Transit and intercity coaches.
cards.evidence_claim: The university offers access to OCCT and Broome County Transit buses, which connect through the downtown area.
cards.access_notes: Open daily for transit services; bus schedules vary by route.

cards.title: Front Street Corridor
cards.subtitle: Front Street
cards.notes: Walk along the Chenango River or access the Binghamton River Trail from this street, which also features several student apartment complexes.
cards.short_summary: A riverside street known for its proximity to parks, the river trail, and various residential options.
cards.evidence_claim: Front Street is located in Binghamton and is near the Binghamton River Trail's 1.5-mile path along the Chenango River.
cards.access_notes: Public street and trail access; parks are typically open from dawn to dusk.

cards.title: Campus Plaza
cards.subtitle: Vestal Parkway East
cards.notes: Find local services like 3j's Hair Salon at this plaza located just west of the main university entrance on the Parkway.
cards.short_summary: A commercial plaza on the Vestal Parkway providing essential services and retail to the student community.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Plaza is located at 3701 Vestal Parkway East and includes businesses like 3j's Hair Salon.
cards.source_title: Local Community Resources List - Binghamton University
cards.access_notes: Open daily for retail and services; business hours vary.
